"33	## Core model
34	
35	Squad-routed work runs through the squad's `leader_id` agent. Consequences:
36	
37	- assigning an issue to a squad routes to the leader;
38	- mentioning a squad routes to the leader;
39	- squad-assigned autopilot resolves to the leader;
40	- squad members are not automatically fanned out;
41	- squad `instructions` are leader briefing content, not member prompts.
42	
43	## CLI
44	
45	Squad commands:
46	
47	```bash
48	multica squad list --output json
49	multica squad get <squad-id> --output json
50	multica squad create --name <name> --leader <agent-name-or-id> --output json
51	multica squad update <squad-id> --instructions "<leader coordination policy>" --output json
52	multica squad delete <squad-id>
53	```
54	
55	Member commands:
56	
57	```bash
58	multica squad member list <squad-id> --output json
59	multica squad member add <squad-id> --member-id <id> --type agent|member --role <role> --output json
60	multica squad member remove <squad-id> --member-id <id> --type agent|member
61	multica squad member set-role <squad-id> --member-id <id> --member-type agent|member --role <role> --output json
62	```
63	
64	Squad leader evaluation command:
65	
66	```bash
67	multica squad activity <issue-id> action|no_action|failed --reason "<why>" --output json
68	```
69	
70	`activity` is a write: it records the leader's evaluation decision on an issue.
71	Use it only when acting as the squad leader after evaluating a trigger.
72	
73	Which issue it accepts: **the issue your current turn is running on**. The
74	target issue does NOT need to be assigned to your squad — a `@squad` mention on
75	an issue owned by an individual agent, or a leader task bound to a child issue,
76	all record fine. What the server checks is your task's leader flag and stamped
77	squad id, not the issue's assignee. A leader woken by a stage barrier runs on
78	the PARENT issue, so record against the parent, not the child you just read;
79	passing an unrelated issue id is rejected and the error names the issue you
80	should have used.
81	
82	If the call fails, do not exit silently — the comment prohibition on `no_action`
83	only applies once the recording succeeded. Post one short comment with the
84	outcome instead, and only when this turn has not already commented: on the
85	`action` path your delegation comment is already that record.
86	
87	Issue/comment commands often needed with squads:
88	
89	```bash
90	multica issue get <issue-id> --output json
91	multica issue update <issue-id> --help
92	multica issue comment list <issue-id> --roots-only --summary --compact --output json
93	multica issue comment add <issue-id> --help
94	```
95	
96	Comment reads stay bounded — the scan-then-expand sequence above, never one
97	unbounded pull.
98	
99	## Squad fields
100	
101	- `id` — squad UUID.
102	- `workspace_id` — workspace the squad belongs to.
103	- `name` — display name; unique per workspace.
104	- `description` — human-facing metadata/display text. Do not assume runtime
105	  prompt impact.
106	- `instructions` — squad-level instructions added to the squad leader briefing.
107	  They are not directly injected into every squad member.
108	- `avatar_url` — optional squad avatar URL.
109	- `leader_id` — agent ID of the squad leader; the runtime target for
110	  squad-routed work.
111	- `creator_id` — creator of the squad.
112	- `archived_at` / `archived_by` — archive metadata. Archived squads are rejected
113	  by assignment/autopilot routing paths.
114	- `member_count` — list response count of squad members.
115	- `member_preview` — list response preview of squad members.
116	
117	Use `instructions` for leader-facing coordination policy: squad responsibility,
118	delegation expectations, when to ask humans, and review/handoff rules. Do not
119	write it as if every member automatically receives it.
120	
121	## Squad member fields
122	
123	- `member_type` — `agent` or `member`.
124	- `member_id` — ID of the agent or workspace member.
125	- `role` — roster role label. A non-empty `role` appears in the leader briefing
126	  roster. It does not create scheduling, permissions, or routing behavior.
127	
128	## Creation and leader membership
129	
130	Creating a squad requires `leader_id`. The leader must be a workspace agent.
131	Create/update does not reject an archived leader: the lookup only checks the
132	agent exists in the workspace. An archived leader fails closed later, at
133	routing/dispatch — assignment, autopilot admission, and the comment/mention
134	readiness gate all reject an archived leader before any task is enqueued.
135	
136	On create, the backend attempts to add the leader as a squad member with role
137	`leader`. When updating `leader_id`, if the new leader is not already a member,
138	the backend adds the new leader as a squad member with role `leader`.
139	
140	## Leader briefing
141	
142	For squad leader tasks, Multica appends a squad leader briefing to the leader
143	agent instructions. The briefing includes:
144	
145	- Squad Operating Protocol;
146	- Squad Roster;
147	- Squad Instructions, only when `instructions` is non-empty.
148	
149	Roster entries include member name, member type, mention markdown, and non-empty
150	role. For agent members the roster also lists their assigned skills
151	(`skills: a, b`, or `no skills assigned` when the agent has none) so the leader
152	can delegate by capability instead of guessing from the role label; human
153	members carry no skills segment. Built-in `multica-*` skills are not listed —
154	only the workspace skills explicitly attached to the agent. Archived agent
155	members are skipped from the briefing roster.
156	
157	## Issue assignment behavior
158	
159	Issues can be assigned to squads with:
160	
161	```text
162	assignee_type = "squad"
163	assignee_id = <squad-id>
164	```
165	
166	Current behavior:
167	
168	- assignment routes work to `squad.leader_id`;
169	- it does not enqueue every squad member;
170	- assignment while status is `backlog` does not immediately start work;
171	- moving a squad-assigned issue out of `backlog` can trigger the leader;
172	- changing assignee cancels existing tasks for the issue before enqueueing the
173	  new assignee path;
174	- parent issue status is agent-managed (same model as direct agent assignment):
175	  the leader's first assignment turn should move the parent to `in_progress`
176	  and keep it there while members work; the leader moves the parent to
177	  `in_review` only when a later re-trigger confirms the overall goal is met.
178	  Completing a leader task (including the first dispatch) does not itself
179	  change issue status;
180	- that status authority is granted only when the issue's `assignee_type` /
181	  `assignee_id` point at THIS squad. The leader briefing is injected on every
182	  leader path, including an `@squad` mention on an issue owned by a plain agent
183	  — on those paths the protocol instead carries an explicit "do not change this
184	  issue's status".
185	
186	The status names above are fixed built-in keys, not categories.
187	
188	Assignment validation rejects a missing type/id pair, non-existent squad,
189	archived squad, archived leader, and private leader when the actor cannot access
190	it.
191	
192	## Comment and mention behavior
193	
194	If an issue is assigned to a squad, a new comment can wake the squad leader. This
195	is leader routing, not member fan-out.
196	
197	A worker's reply also wakes the assigned leader without an explicit mention. If
198	the leader's current run started before the reply arrived, the reply is
199	delivered in a follow-up run after that run completes, so the worker does not
200	need to mention the leader again.
201	
202	Squad mention format:
203	
204	```md
205	[@Squad Name](mention://squad/<squad-id>)
206	```
